claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating has stable wear resistance and a high elastic modulus at 300 K.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating is an FCC solid solution.
The coating has a nanocrystalline or fine-grained microstructure.
At 300 K, lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening suppress dislocation mobility in FeNiCrCoCu.
A stable, high dislocation density at 300 K facilitates strain hardening and wear resistance.
Increasing temperature thermally activates dislocation motion by reducing the effective Peierls barrier.
High-strain elevated-temperature loading in Al0.1CrCoFeNi exhibits a thermo-plastic instability analogous to that proposed for FeNiCrCoCu.
The Al0.1CrCoFeNi analogy specifically supports a transition from defect-mediated plasticity to rapid lattice disordering.
Loss of local or short-range order lowers yield strength and elastic modulus by weakening solid-solution strengthening.
The critical temperature is reached when thermal energy overcomes ordering-energy barriers.
Crossing the critical temperature causes cascading dislocation multiplication and stacking-fault coalescence.
Dislocation multiplication, stacking-fault accumulation, and dislocation tangling produce localized shear bands.
Above the critical temperature, a tangled and unstable dislocation network facilitates rapid material removal and catastrophic wear.
For FeNiCrCoCu, the critical temperature lies between 450 K and 600 K.
Above the critical temperature, wear rate will increase by orders of magnitude and the coefficient of friction will become unstable.
Above the critical temperature, dislocation density will exhibit a nonlinear spike.
Increasing temperature will decrease stacking-fault energy, promoting planar slip and shear localization.
Formation of a protective oxide layer can prevent the proposed high-temperature wear collapse, as suggested for AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
The Cu-matrix interface, strain rate, and surface roughness can alter the value or sharpness of the transition temperature.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis and predicted outcome describe a sharp threshold and sharp wear decline, whereas the uncertainty field allows the transition to be gradual.
